newsitem.title: USA: Station Casinos $150 mln junk bond deal postponed.
newsitem.headline: Station Casinos $150 mln junk bond deal postponed.

text.p: BancAmerica Securities Inc has postponed an offering of $150 million in Station Casinos Inc junk bonds until May due to poor market conditions, a BancAmerica Securities source said.
"We recognized that with the stock market being pounded, this is just not a good time to bring a deal," he said.

The postponment puts the underwriter in a risky position as BancAmerica Securities, a subsidiary of BankAmerica Corp, has committed to buying the $150 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes from Station, market analysts said.

"If we had known the stock market was going to go down an additional (391 points in the last three sessions), we probably would have taken a deeper breath and probably asked the client for slightly cheaper pricing," the source added.
"But we would have done the same thing ... that is what any world-class financial institution ought to be prepared to do for its very best clients," he said.
The BancAmerica Securities source declined to reveal the price at which the underwriter bought the bonds. He said that information would be disclosed after the deal was priced.
Price talk on the bonds was originally 10.125 percent to 10.25 percent, he confirmed.
Some junk bond players said BancAmerica was unwise to have committed its capital in such an open manner prior to marketing the deal.
"When the world knew that BancAmerica was long these bonds, they instantly had more leverage. This was the wrong market to be buying a deal in," said one analyst.
The BancAmerica source said the underwriter does not plan to conduct a roadshow to sell the junk bonds in May.
Instead, he said the underwriter plans to arrange one-on-one meetings with potential investors and Station officials, who will explain that the company is committed to very significant deleveraging.
He said Station officials will also be speaking at two high-yield conferences in mid-April hosted by Bear, Stearns & Co Inc and Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette Securities Corp.
Station is a Las Vegas-based casino company that owns and operates facilities in Nevada and Missouri.
